concise_definition: Opportunistic central nervous system infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii that produces intracranial lesions.
time_course: Subacute
severity_or_acuity: Urgent
epidemiology_summary: Occurs predominantly with advanced cellular immunosuppression.
risk_factors_summary: Advanced HIV infection or other severe cellular immunosuppression.
pathophysiology_summary: Reactivation of latent Toxoplasma gondii in brain tissue produces focal inflammatory lesions.
classic_presentation_summary: Subacute headache focal neurologic deficit seizure or altered mental status in an immunocompromised host.
key_distinguishing_features: Brain lesions require differentiation from primary CNS lymphoma and other opportunistic infections in the host context.
common_board_traps: Ring enhancement is not specific to toxoplasmosis.
emergency_red_flags: Declining consciousness seizures progressive focal deficit or concern for mass effect requires urgent evaluation.
disposition_summary: Urgent neuroimaging and specialty-directed management are appropriate when suspected.
prognosis_summary: Outcome depends on immune status lesion burden and timely pathogen-directed therapy.
notes: Source-supported cerebral toxoplasmosis canonical record.
subject_exams: Neurology; Internal Medicine; Infectious Disease; Emergency Medicine

concise_definition: Stable angina is a clinically distinct cardiology entity: Myocardial oxygen supply-demand mismatch or acute coronary obstruction produces ischemia.
time_course: acute when symptoms evolve over minutes to days; chronic phenotypes require longitudinal assessment
severity_or_acuity: emergent when perfusion, oxygenation, or electrical stability is threatened

disposition_summary: Acute ischemic syndromes need monitored emergency evaluation and reperfusion-capable consultation when indicated.
prognosis_summary: Outcome depends on infarct size, timely reperfusion, ventricular function, and complications.

prognosis_summary: Prognosis is benign in typical reflex syncope but worsens sharply with structural heart disease or malignant arrhythmia.

time_course: acute when symptoms evolve over minutes to days; chronic phenotypes require longitudinal assessment
severity_or_acuity: emergent when perfusion, oxygenation, or electrical stability is threatened
epidemiology_summary: Structural heart disease, ischemia, electrolyte disturbance, stimulants, medications, inherited channelopathy, and hypoxia can precipitate rhythm disease.
risk_factors_summary: Structural heart disease, ischemia, electrolyte disturbance, stimulants, medications, inherited channelopathy, and hypoxia can precipitate rhythm disease.
pathophysiology_summary: Abnormal impulse formation or conduction alters rate, rhythm, and cardiac output.
classic_presentation_summary: Palpitations, presyncope, syncope, chest discomfort, or dyspnea may occur; some rhythms are incidental.
key_distinguishing_features: ECG rhythm morphology, QRS width, regularity, pre-excitation, QT interval, and stability determine the safe pathway.

disposition_summary: Unstable perfusing tachyarrhythmia requires synchronized cardioversion; pulseless VF or VT requires defibrillation and CPR.
prognosis_summary: Risk ranges from benign ectopy to sudden death; structural heart disease and inherited syndromes change risk.

severity_or_acuity: emergent when airway, perfusion, consciousness, vision, or progressive neurologic function is threatened

disposition_summary: Status needs immediate stabilization and sequential antiseizure treatment; a first event needs cause-focused disposition.

severity_or_acuity: Emergent when neurovascular compromise, sepsis, compartment physiology, unstable trauma, spinal compression, or threatened limb is present.

risk_factors_summary: Repetitive load, pivoting trauma, training error, age, and altered biomechanics influence risk.
pathophysiology_summary: Tendon, ligament, meniscal, or periarticular injury produces location-specific pain, weakness, instability, or mechanical symptoms.
classic_presentation_summary: Localize pain, swelling, deformity, stiffness, weakness, gait change, range-of-motion loss, and systemic findings before selecting tests.
